checkpoints.description: [1/1] measurement invalidated the first plan: no implementation started, decision is with the user. Unit 1.21s/317 tests is 1047 real file opens (0.37s); cached repo reads save only 55ms of the 250-450ms gap, and the rest is ledger atomicity/locking I/O that PRINCIPLE-013 requires to be real. Integration 7.76s/45 tests has a 3.49s floor from 35 real CLI spawns (100ms each) plus real git work; the slowest test already uses a trivial nested test command. Neither tier reaches its budget by removing waste alone.

impact_assessment.why: PRINCIPLE-003 requires the plan to rest on measurement, and the measurement refuted the caching lever before any file was edited
impact_assessment.benefits: no speculative refactor was committed; the remaining routes are named with numbers so the user can choose
impact_assessment.risks: contract: closing the gap now needs either weaker atomicity tests (PRINCIPLE-014 needs user approval plus an ADR) or an amended budget in PRINCIPLE-010/014 (PRINCIPLE-000 R3 cross-principle check); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: task stays in_progress with zero edits, so the tree is still the committed b4f9582
impact_assessment.mitigation: stop at Phase 2, report the measurements and the three routes, and re-plan as a new [1/M] checkpoint once the user picks one

checkpoints.description: [1/4] scripts/check_test_budgets.py runs both tiers and enforces a per-test average, with failing-first tests pinning the breach path; [2/4] amend PRINCIPLE-010 and PRINCIPLE-014 to per-test budgets naming the gate, then sync_principles regenerates the 8 Tier 1 targets, the README table and SKILL.md; [3/4] README gate table and tree, runbook Phase 4 list, ADR-144 with its cross-principle check, knowledge base refresh; [4/4] Phase 4 gates and delivery

impact_assessment.why: the user chose route B: the absolute per-suite wall clock (<1s, <5s) cannot hold as the suite grows, and nothing measured it, so the overrun drifted in unnoticed; a per-test average preserves the intent of fast feedback and is enforceable
impact_assessment.benefits: budgets become measured instead of assumed; the gate reports the per-test average on every run; unit 3.59-5.84ms and integration 169.6-176.5ms both pass with headroom
impact_assessment.risks: contract: this relaxes a stated budget, so the ADR must name the user's approval (PRINCIPLE-014 R3) and carry a cross-principle check over all 20 principles (PRINCIPLE-000 R3); dependency: standard library only; concurrency: the gate must not run the tiers twice per Phase 4 or it doubles the cost it measures; state: the gate only reads, it writes no ledger or repository file
impact_assessment.mitigation: ceilings set from three measured runs including a cold-cache outlier (8ms and 200ms, 37% and 13% headroom); the gate becomes the single way Phase 4 runs the tiers rather than an extra run; PRINCIPLE-018 R3 item (1) still reads 'both test tiers pass', so its text needs no edit

impact_assessment.why: the pre-commit triad runs on the working tree, so a commit can contain less than what was tested: ADR-145 was committed without its implementation and a stale codebase map was committed twice today
impact_assessment.benefits: a broken commit is caught while it is still local, where PRINCIPLE-018 R5 undoes it with reset --soft instead of a revert, and the pushed history stays green for bisect and for anyone who checks out that commit
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new script and a new P018 rule; dependency: git worktree (already used by the kit's own tooling); concurrency: the worktree lives in the system temp dir, never inside the repository; state: none, the worktree is removed in a finally block
impact_assessment.mitigation: runner injected so unit tests spawn nothing; worktree removed even when a gate fails; one real end-to-end run recorded as evidence; integration test kept to the --help contract so the tier ceiling holds
